ankle_flex.source: Gravitus Seated Calf Raise: "Lower your heels as far as comfortably possible to create a stretch in the soleus muscle" (illustrative 15 degrees of dorsiflexion, no exact angle given); push up onto the toes as high as possible (illustrative -35 degrees of plantar flexion), inside the AAOS ankle row

knee_flex.source: Gravitus Seated Calf Raise: "Maintain your knees at approximately 90 degrees throughout the movement, not allowing them to rise or extend"; "Focus on using only your ankle joint movement - avoid lifting with your knees or hips"

muscles.peakSource: Gravitus Seated Calf Raise: the rep uses only ankle-joint movement to push up "as high as possible," so calf effort is highest approaching and through that top contraction

mistake.name: Bounce and shortchange it

tells.text: The heels bounce off the bottom stretch instead of pausing there.
The rise stops halfway instead of reaching full plantar flexion.

mistake.source: Hevy Seated Calf Raises: "bouncing takes the tension away from the calves and instead forces our Achilles tendons to absorb the force"; using too much weight "prevents them from doing the full range of motion... each repetition lacks a solid stretch"

sources: Contact fact (knee pad / footplate): the padded lever rests just above the knees while the balls of the feet sit on the footplate, heels hanging off the edge (Gravitus)
